instruction.text: Find the examples of stone-age medicine.

atoms.b: In the ((++Stone Wood)) Age, people believed that illnesses were evil spirits in the body.
Stone-age surgeons would make holes using stone ((++hammers hedgehogs)) and flint knives to let the spirits out.

hint.label: Flint
hint.text: Flint is a type of rock that can be broken to make sharp edges.

atoms.b: Cutting a hole in someone’s ((++head shed)) was a common, if very painful, way of curing headaches!

instruction.text: Stone-age people also had some knowledge of healing. Drag the items to the wound.

feedback.finish: Stone-age people understood that some herbs had healing effects, like reducing soreness and preventing infection.

instruction.text: Stone-age people also had some knowledge of healing. Drag the items to the wound.

feedback.finish: Mud was used to protect open wounds from infection — just like you might use a plaster! Some people also ate mineral-rich clay because they saw animals doing it to get better.

instruction.text: Match the descriptions of stone-age medicine to the correct images.

feedback.finish: When practical medicine failed, stone-age people often turned to their religions for help. People would travel to places like Stonehenge because they thought that magic there would heal them.

instruction.text: Do you think stone-age medicine was better than what we have today?

feedback.end: While they did the best they could, stone-age medicine wasn’t able to help a lot of people. Even common illnesses like the flu would have been very dangerous for them.
